cards.src_text: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
cards.tgt_text: And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.
cards.note: 1 John 2:3 — *And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.* *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.* (Matthew 28:20) The last word of the gospel is *teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you*. John tells how anyone can know whether that word took: *if we keep his commandments*. The commission and the test are the same thing seen from two ends. What the taught are to observe is what the knower keeps; there is no knowing him apart from it.

cards.src_text: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
cards.tgt_text: By this we know that we love the children of Elohim (God), when we love Elohim (God), and keep his commandments.
cards.old_note: *This is the love of Elohim, that we keep his commandments.*
cards.note: 1 John 5:2 — *By this we know that we love the children of Elohim (God), when we love Elohim (God), and keep his commandments.* *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.* (Matthew 28:20) *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you* is not a cold rule laid on the gathered. John names what the keeping is: love of Elohim (God) and love of his children are known *when we love Elohim (God), and keep his commandments*. The observing the commission asks for is the shape love takes; where the commandments are dropped, the love has nothing to stand in.

cards.src_text: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.
cards.tgt_text: And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:
cards.old_note: John 5:14 — *Afterward Yahusha (Jesus) findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.* *Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 18:19) The man he made whole is told *sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee*. What the Father does at the Son's hand comes with the commandment, *My Father worketh hitherto, and I work* (John 5:17), so what two agree to ask is not a blank cheque for anything at all.
cards.note: 1 John 5:14 — *And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:* *Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 18:19) Two who agree on earth about what they ask will have it done *of my Father which is in heaven*. John sets the measure that goes with the promise: what is asked *according to his will* is what he hears. The agreement of two is not a lever on heaven; it is two hearts asking what the Father already wills, and that asking he hears.
